title: Prelude in E minor, Op. 28 No. 4 ("Largo")
trains: Chromatic voice leading, sustained dissonance, a wide dynamic range, and rhythmic independence between a slow-moving right-hand line and pulsing left-hand chords.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Frédéric Chopin, Prelude in E minor, Op. 28 No. 4 (composed 1839, public domain; Chopin died 1849). Pitches and rhythm were checked measure-by-measure against the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond engraving (piece-info id 468) before this original engraving was made.
provenance.note: Complete piece: the 1-eighth-note pickup plus all 25 bars, ending on the closing perfect cadence in E minor. Slurs, pedal markings, hairpins and the closing fermatas of the source engraving are omitted from this file; they do not change the sounding pitches or rhythm. Independent review (2026-09-22) confirmed every pitch bar by bar against the Mutopia source, with one disclosed low-confidence detail: the left-hand chord's bass note in measure 24 (of this file's 0-indexed pickup-as-0 numbering; Chopin's own bar 23) is written B2 - the reviewer's two independent derivations of that one note (from a cross-staff voice in the source engraving) did not fully agree on its octave, though both agree on the pitch class (B, the dominant), so this is a possible octave nuance in one inner voice, not a wrong note.

limitations: Pedal is not written or played; performers commonly sustain this prelude with continuous pedal, which this file does not encode.
